prompt:
You are given a literature matrix with {n_rows} rows covering {n_articles} reports of randomized controlled trials. Each row has a row id (like R0001), an article id (like PMC1234567), an INTERVENTION, a COMPARATOR and an OUTCOME, all copied from the matrix. For every row, fill in what that article reports for the OUTCOME in the INTERVENTION group relative to the COMPARATOR group.

There are exactly three allowed values. "increased" means the article reports the outcome measure is statistically significantly higher with the intervention than with the comparator. "decreased" means significantly lower. "no_difference" means the article reports no statistically significant difference between the two groups for that outcome.

The direction is about the value of the outcome measure, not about whether it is good or bad for patients: for example, significantly less pain is "decreased". The intervention is always compared against the comparator, in that order, even if the article describes the groups the other way round. Statistical significance is as the article reports it (p-values, confidence intervals, or the authors' significance statements). The answer must come from the article's own text, which includes results sections and tables, not only the abstract.

The only source is the article collection available through the tools; there is no internet access. Use list_rows to page through the matrix, list_articles to see article ids with titles and lengths, and read_article to read article text in chunks. Do not rely on titles or abstracts alone; read enough of each article to find the reported comparison for every outcome in its rows. Work through all {n_rows} rows; each of the {n_articles} reports may contribute several rows.

A row is judged together with the other rows of the same article: an article counts as done only if all of its rows are filled correctly.

Final answer: one JSON object mapping every row id to one of the three values, for example {"R0001": "decreased", "R0002": "no_difference"}. Rows that are missing count as wrong.
tool_list_rows: Pages through the matrix rows; call it with an offset and a limit to see each row's id, article id, INTERVENTION, COMPARATOR and OUTCOME.
tool_list_articles: Pages through the article ids with their titles and lengths, using offset and limit, so you can plan which articles to read.
tool_read_article: Reads an article's text starting from a character offset, returning up to a limit of characters. Articles are about 25,000 characters long, so most take several reads.
unit_prompt:
You are given {n_rows} rows of a literature matrix, all from the article {article}. Each row has a row id (like R0001), an INTERVENTION, a COMPARATOR and an OUTCOME. For every row, decide what the article reports for the OUTCOME in the INTERVENTION group relative to the COMPARATOR group, using only the article's own text (results sections and tables, not only the abstract); there is no internet access.

Exactly three values are allowed: "increased" means the outcome measure is statistically significantly higher with the intervention than with the comparator; "decreased" means significantly lower; "no_difference" means no statistically significant difference. Direction concerns the value of the measure, not whether it is good or bad (significantly less pain is "decreased"); the intervention is always compared against the comparator, in that order, even if the article reverses them. Significance is as the article reports it.

Final answer: one JSON object mapping every row id to one value, e.g. {"R0001": "decreased", "R0002": "no_difference"}. Missing rows count as wrong.
